subject: Discovery recap: Observability & Evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Janet Li <janet.li@zenhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, elliot.price@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & Evals — next steps

Hi Janet —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Lack of per-route/per-model observability: hard to tell which prompts or model variants drive latency/cost spikes.
- Surface-level alerts only; no regression detection for prompt-level quality drift.
- Rollouts cause sometimes-unexpected quality regressions; limited guardrails for automated fallbacks.

Current stack you described:
- Primary LLMs hosted via third-party managed endpoints (mix of open and private variants)
- Monitoring: metrics in Datadog (service-level, high-level latency), logs in Elastic
- No dedicated eval harness; manual spot-checks for releases

Success criteria (what would make this project a win):
1) Dashboarding: latency, p99, token cost per route/model version, error rates by model version; golden-prompt regression dashboard that ties eval scores to deploys.
2) Tracing hooks: per-request tracing that lets you map latency/cost back to prompt template and user route.
3) Eval artifacts: golden prompt sets + small ground-truth eval datasets to run nightly regression checks.
4) Rollout guardrails: canary policies + automatic fallback to previous model variant on regression or latency SLO breach.

What Redwood can deliver (proposed):
- Observability dashboard templates (latency by model/route, cost-per-token, regression alerts) — we can provide sample dashboards for Datadog or our Console.
- Tracing integrations: lightweight request headers + tracing hooks to surface prompt templates and model metadata in each trace.
- Evals plan: nightly evaluation harness running golden prompts + customizable metrics (F1, BLEU-like metrics where applicable, prompt-anchored quality signals).
- Rollout guardrails and policies: canary thresholds, auto-fallback, and alerting tie-ins to PagerDuty/Slack.

Attachments: I attached a draft eval plan (redwood-eval-plan-draft.pdf) and a sample golden prompt CSV schema.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the success criteria above (reply with any corrections).
2) We share a short technical checklist for your infra team (required tracing headers, sample payloads).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer (we proposed Wed 24 Feb 10:00 PT below).
4) Exchange the minimal eval dataset (we can accept a redacted sample) and get a DPA signed if needed.

Would Wednesday 24 Feb at 10:00 PT work for a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra and ML engineering folks?

Thanks again — looping in Rishi (success criteria / evals) and Elliot (rollout guardrails) on next steps.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Marissa —

This is great — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items you captured. A few notes and answers to your proposed next steps: 

Confirmations / additions:
- Dashboards we care about (priority order): 1) latency by model & route (p50/p95/p99), 2) token cost per request & per-route cost breakdown, 3) regression dashboard tied to golden prompts, 4) error rate by model version.
- We can provide a small, redacted eval dataset (~500 examples) and a sample golden prompt set. I attached the golden prompts CSV we currently use (golden-prompts.csv) — it’s a small list but should be enough for an initial regression harness.
- Tracing: we can add a tracing header and forward request metadata; our infra engineer will want the header names and sample payloads.

Procurement / timeline:
- Procurement: we’re aiming to complete vendor evaluation and procurement by end of Q1 (target decision week of Mar 23).
- Stakeholders: me (Product), Michael Grant (CTO), and Priya (ML Eng lead). We’ll want a short exec summary for Michael after the tech deep-dive.

Scheduling:
- Wed Feb 24 10:00 PT works for the tech deep-dive — please send a calendar invite. Attendees from our side: Janet, Priya, one infra engineer.

Legal/data: please send the DPA / Data Processing Addendum link; we usually sign via DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Janet Li
Head of Product, ZenHealth
janet.li@zenhealth.com
